key_insight: A hybrid symbolic–numerical–PINN framework computes geodesics and visualizes geodesic spheres for the three-dimensional Riemannian metric g = diag(1, x², 1), x > 0.
engineering_relevance: The workflow supports geometry-aware scientific computing by pairing learned differential-equation solutions with conventional numerical integration.
method: Symbolically compute Christoffel symbols and curvature tensors.
Solve geodesic equations using SciPy integration and a physics-informed neural network.
Visualize geodesic spheres and numerically estimate intrinsic surface area and volume.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports PINN–SciPy comparison and grid refinement; at base resolution, radius-one sphere area and ball volume are approximately 0.362% and 0.364% below Euclidean values, respectively.
watch_item: This metric is locally flat, so visual deformation and small area/volume deficits require coordinate, domain, and discretization checks before being attributed to intrinsic curvature.
paper_title: A Physics-Informed Neural Network for Geodesic Computation and Visualization of Geodesic Spheres on Riemannian Manifolds
